title: iTaskSense: Task-Oriented Object Detection in Resource-Constrained Environments
problem: Efficient task-oriented object detection on edge/resource-constrained devices; conventional models require extensive datasets and struggle with generalization to diverse real-world scenarios.
motivation: Autonomous systems (drones, vehicles, healthcare, industrial) need efficient intelligent sensing; vision-language models have high computational cost; edge devices require low-latency, efficient task-specific detection.
method: The system uses large language models (AI trained on massive amounts of text) to learn from just a few examples by building knowledge graphs that map out task-specific requirements and attributes. It provides two different vision transformers (neural networks for image recognition): one specialized and compressed for particular tasks, achieving 15% higher accuracy on those specific tasks, and another heavily compressed version (quantized—reducing precision to shrink size) that works across multiple different tasks with reasonable performance. A custom hardware acceleration circuit enables these models to run directly on edge devices (resource-constrained hardware like phones or sensors) for real-time processing without sending data to the cloud.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using large language models to automatically generate task-specific knowledge graphs that enable object detection from just a few examples, paired with two different vision transformers (one optimized for accuracy on specific tasks, another compressed for flexibility across tasks) and a custom hardware circuit for real-time edge processing.
contributions: iTask framework leveraging LLMs to generate abstract knowledge graphs for task-specific detection
Dual-configuration approach: task-specific distilled ViT and quantized multi-task ViT
Custom hardware accelerator for edge real-time processing
3.5x speedup and 40% energy reduction vs. GPU-based implementations

metrics.accuracy: 15% higher accuracy in task-specific configuration over quantized baseline

primary_theme: Task-oriented object detection on edge devices via LLM knowledge graphs and hardware acceleration
